transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Priya (SE) and Samir (CSM). Quick soundcheck?
[00:10] Maya Thompson: Hi Jordan, hear you, thanks.
[00:14] Carlos Ruiz: Good here.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Great, I'll jump in on tech details as we go.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Objective for today: align on goals and success criteria for the onboarding, cover security and network constraints, and agree next steps and owners. I'll hand to Maya to kick off with your priorities.
[00:30] Maya Thompson: Sure. We want Redwood to power two immediate features: in-app summarization for clinician notes (real-time, low-latency) and a background batch rerank/embedding job for search. Top constraints are data residency and encryption; Ben is here for security. Timeline: ideally pilot in 4 weeks, production in 8-10 weeks if benchmarks look good.
[00:50] Ben Ortiz: For security, SOC 2 scope is required, also SSO with our IdP (SAML), and we use AWS KMS for key management. We need audit logs for all inference calls and data retention controls.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Perfect — Redwood supports SSO SAML and has SOC 2. We also offer audit logs and integrations with KMS, and there are options for Private (VPC) deployment if you need a customer-managed network. Priya, do you want to add on deployment choices?
[01:20] Priya Nair: Yeah quick high-level: we have three modes — Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Private VPC/on-prem. For your latency needs on real-time clinician summarization, Dedicated or Private usually gives the most predictable p99 latency; Hosted can still work if you want fastest time-to-value but there's more variability. We can do a canary model on Hosted first, then flip to Dedicated as needed.
[01:45] Carlos Ruiz: The latency target is p95 < 300ms for short notes (avg token length ~120). Is that realistic?
[01:52] Priya Nair: With Dedicated and optimized batching + KV caching, yes. We'll need to set the right sequence length, quantization profile, and batching policy. Our SE benchmark plan will show expected throughput/latency numbers.
[02:08] Alicia Kim: On network, we prefer VPC peering and no public egress from our subnet. Can Redwood support strict egress rules and IP allowlists?
[02:15] Samir Patel: Yes, we support allowlist and VPC peering for Private or Dedicated deployed into customer VPC. For Hosted, we can provide static egress IPs and IP allowlist options for your firewall.
[02:28] Ben Ortiz: Also key rotation — we manage keys in AWS KMS, can we rotate keys without downtime?
[02:33] Priya Nair: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM and support key wrapping and rotation. There is a small config step; we can document the flow. We'll include that in the security doc.
[02:45] Carlos Ruiz: For data retention — we need to ensure customer data isn't persisted beyond 30 days for pilot. Is that configurable?
[02:52] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention policies are configurable per project; we also have options to disable long-term storage and only keep ephemeral logs for debugging. We'll share the retention settings doc.
[03:05] Maya Thompson: On ML side — embeddings for search: we're evaluating vector DBs. Will Redwood handle embedding generation and send vectors to our DB, or do you recommend a partner?
[03:15] Priya Nair: Redwood generates embeddings via the API; you can stream them to your vector store. We don't replace vector DBs; we integrate well with most (we've seen customers use Pinecone, Weaviate, etc.). If you want, our SEs can run throughput tests for embedding generation.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: Quick commercial note — there are usage-based pricing tiers for Hosted and committed pricing for Dedicated. We'll send a pricing sheet after this call.
[03:40] Leah Park: Who's the main contact for weekly updates?
[03:43] Samir Patel: I'll be the CSM and run weekly cadence. First weekly check-in proposed for 2026-09-16.
[03:50] Jordan Lee: Let's get into the pilot scope — Priya?
[03:53] Priya Nair: For pilot we recommend: two APIs: (1) real-time summarization endpoint configured with a shorter context window and KV cache, target p95 < 300ms, sample RPS 10-20; (2) batch embeddings job for nightly rerank, throughput oriented. We'll run a small benchmark with your sample traffic and model configurations.
[04:15] Carlos Ruiz: What model variants are available? We need to balance cost vs quality, could we use a smaller quantized model for background jobs?
[04:22] Priya Nair: Yes, we can recommend quantized variants and lower-cost model for batch embeddings. For the clinician-facing summarization we usually stick with the higher-quality model. We'll include model recommendations in the benchmark deck.
[04:36] Ben Ortiz: On compliance, we have additional audit requirements — can you provide SOC 2 report and a data processing addendum?
[04:44] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 and DPAs. I'll attach them to the CRM and email.
[04:50] Maya Thompson: Can we do a short technical deep dive next week — network + performance?
[04:54] Priya Nair: Absolutely — I'll set up a SE-led session to run through the benchmark plan and required test harness.
[04:59] Carlos Ruiz: About rollout — after pilot, how long to get Dedicated capacity?
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Dedicated provisioning lead time depends on capacity but typically 2-4 weeks once contract and commit are in place. We can also do Hosted with a reserved pool to speed things up.
[05:13] Alicia Kim: Any standard runbook for incident escalation and support SLAs? We need a primary contact and an on-call for severity 1s.
[05:20] Samir Patel: We provide an enterprise support add-on with SLA and a named technical account manager. We'll include the support appendix in the contract.
[05:28] Ben Ortiz: One minor note — sometimes transcriptions and model args get mistranscribed in docs, watch for "KV cash" typos etc.
[05:33] Priya Nair: (laughs) Noted. We'll be careful.
[05:36] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap of decisions: pilot scope agreed (summarization + embeddings), security requirements documented (SOC2, SAML, KMS, retention), SE benchmark next week, weekly CSM cadence starting 2026-09-16, pricing and onboarding docs to be sent.
[05:55] Maya Thompson: That sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: Thanks — we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[06:02] [meeting end]
